name: Flares — venue-anchored ephemeral stories that ARE the map's heat
firstPrinciple: A story is not media, it is a decaying, geofence-verified liveness signal anchored to a venue. Every story literally raises a venue's visible temperature, and the only way to view a story is through the map — so posting = "putting this place on the map," viewing = discovery, and replying = going. No story tab, no feed, no person-anchored content, ever (aggregate-only heat is a thesis non-negotiable).
coreLoop: See a venue glowing with a live story-ring → tap the pin → watch the aggregated place-reel (friends' clips first, then circles, then public) answering the go/no-go questions (crowd, music, line, £-spend chip from Decision 007) → one-tap action from the reel: "OMW" (live ETA shared to your circle), "Pool us in" (deep-link to a group→group Pool invite with the poster's group), or directions → arrive, geofence unlocks the composer → "Drop a flare — put Archive 9 on the map" (2-tap capture) → your flare brightens the venue's ring and heat → pulls the next viewer out the door. Closed loop: see → go → post → pull; the success metric is arrivals produced per story, not views.
mapStructure: Four altitudes, stories rendered differently at each; the map is never left — everything above city view is an overlay on the map camera. (1) WORLD (night-globe, Decision 006): no individual stories — city nodes gain a shimmer proportional to live flare volume and the global counter reads "Velmont · 214 out · 38 flares live." Aggregate only; tapping a city dives to city view. (2) CITY (SVG Velmont): the heat gradient itself is partly story-driven (see heat model); venues with live stories wear a segmented neon story-ring around their pin — segment count = fresh clips, ring brightness = recency (full neon <2h, dimming to ember by 6h, gone after). Friend groups co-located at a venue fuse into a Gathering Pin (Zenly's load-bearing mechanic) that wears an avatar-stack story ring when any member has posted — "your mates are together at Vespers AND documenting it" is the peak FOMO object and out-ranks every other pin in size. A thin map-derived "Tonight near you" rail (bottom edge, not a tab) lists the 3–5 hottest ringed venues by recency × proximity × volume; tapping an entry flies the map camera to that pin — the rail is an index into the map, never a separate surface. (3) VENUE CARD (tap a ringed pin): mini-card gains a filmstrip of story thumbnails newest-first, live stats (level, groups in the pool, avg spend), and an "en route" avatar row of circle members who tapped OMW. (4) REEL (tap filmstrip): full-screen overlay that keeps map context persistent — venue name, distance, cost chip and the action bar (OMW / Pool us in / hype) pinned at all times; clips auto-advance through the merged place-reel (aggregation over authorship — you're watching the PLACE); swipe down drops you back onto the map exactly where you were. Movement: pinch world↔city, tap pin→card→reel, swipe-down unwinds one level.

keyFeatures.how: Capture unlocks only inside a recognized venue's geofence at night — you can only put a place on the map FROM the place. Two taps: shoot → post (audience defaults to Circles). Prompted, not nagged: one prompt on arrival-dwell (>20 min) and one when your RSVP'd event starts. Post-night, all your group's flares auto-collect into a private group recap (Partiful lesson) — memory is downstream, the map only ever shows live content.
keyFeatures.ceoQuestions: WHERE CAPTURED: at venues only, with a post-night private recap; this also guarantees every story is spatially interesting (BeReal's bedroom-content failure is impossible by construction).

keyFeatures.how: Stories surface exclusively as rings on venue pins, avatar-ringed Gathering Pins for co-located friend groups, city-node shimmer at world altitude, and the map-derived Tonight rail. There is no ring row at the top of a list and no stories tab — the inspiration artifact's top-of-list ring is explicitly rejected as separate-surface (its critique doc's weakness #5); its spot-tagged composer is kept but hardened from a self-declared tag to geofence proof.
keyFeatures.ceoQuestions: WHERE SURFACED: venue pins, friend presence, world view — all on the one centrepiece surface, satisfying the map-first directive and the Snap Map 5-second-legibility bar (pin + ring + heat needs zero tutorial).

keyFeatures.feature: Fast-decay lifespan tuned to a night out
keyFeatures.how: Hot for 2 hours (full ring + full heat weight), cooling ember from 2–6h (dimmer, still in reel, half heat weight), gone from the map at 6h or the venue's close, archived to the poster's private recap at 24h. Nightlife's relevance horizon is ~2h, not Instagram's 24 — a stale story that pulls someone to a dead bar destroys trust in the whole map, so freshness must be visually legible (ring brightness) not just timestamped.
keyFeatures.ceoQuestions: LIFESPAN: decaying liveness signal, not a gallery; the cooling visual doubles as the freshness UI.

keyFeatures.feature: Reply→action loop: OMW and Pool-us-in, no cold DMs
keyFeatures.how: The reply bar has exactly three verbs: (1) OMW — one tap shares your live ETA with your own circle and adds you to the venue card's en-route row (the pre-arrival phase is the real coordination pain); (2) Pool us in — if the poster's group has an open invite tonight, the reply deep-links into a prefilled group→group Pool request, so a story converts into Func's hero mechanic; (3) emoji hype (costless, opens no channel). Stranger replies route to the poster's GROUP, never a 1:1 DM — this upgrades the inspiration artifact's individual→table 'Join' into group-accepts-group, which is simultaneously the product mechanic and the safety architecture per the thesis.
keyFeatures.ceoQuestions: REPLY→ACTION: a story's terminal state is a person out the door or a Pool invite, and 'arrivals per story' becomes the ranking signal — a night out is the success metric, not views.

keyFeatures.how: Viewing and posting both sit behind the launch 18+ ID check. Audience per flare: My Group / Circles (groups + earned friends, the default) / The City (public opt-in, pooled into the place-reel where authorship is secondary). Stories pin to the VENUE point, never the poster's coordinates — leaving the venue changes nothing, so a flare is proof-of-was-here, not a tracker ('this bar is popping' is discovery; 'this person is here' is the Instagram-2025 backlash headline). One-toggle time-boxed Ghost Mode (tonight / 3h / until-off) hides presence independently of posting. Face-blur tool in the composer, one-tap report on every clip, women-first safety review before ship, OMW visibility strictly circle-gated so it can never become pursuit.
keyFeatures.ceoQuestions: PRIVACY: 18+ and circles handled as architecture, not settings; preserves the aggregate-only-heat non-negotiable.

keyFeatures.feature: Stories feed the heat layer (and the moat)
keyFeatures.how: Venue heat = venue baseline (historical busyness — the never-blank cold-start floor) + aggregate presence + event RSVPs + story signal, where story signal = clips × recency with a ~90-min exponential half-life, and is the highest-weighted live term because geofenced flares are verified presence. Anti-gaming: per-user-per-venue nightly contribution cap, poster standing weighting (hooks into Vouch — a flare from a well-vouched regular counts more), venue/staff accounts labelled and down-weighted, reciprocal hype discounted. Because the heat is generated BY your social layer, it compounds with the network — the structural gap Current/NOITE/afterhours cannot cross.
keyFeatures.ceoQuestions: HEAT FEED: every story is a heat input with a decay curve; also seeds the Snap-validated roadmap (heat → places → loyalty → promoted placement = the B2B2C revenue line).

firstTimeUserStory: Friday, 9:40pm. A new user with zero friends on Func opens the app onto the Velmont map. Three venues are visibly glowing; one — Archive 9 in The Arches — has a bright segmented ring pulsing around its pin. No tutorial needed: hot colours mean busy, the ring means live footage. She taps the pin (0:15): mini-card shows "Level 3 · 3 groups in the pool tonight · £25ish night" and a filmstrip of six fresh clips. She taps the filmstrip (0:25): a full-screen reel of strangers' 15-second clips from the last hour — packed floor, the DJ, a short line — with the venue name, "12 min away" and the action bar pinned below. By 0:50 she knows exactly what tonight looks like there. She taps OMW — or notices "Pool us in" because one of the clip-posting groups has an open invite, and sends her group's first Pool request straight from the story. Sixty seconds in, the map has answered "where is actually good tonight" and handed her a next step — single-player useful on day one, exactly the cold-start promise in the thesis.
differentiators: Stories exist ONLY on the map — no tab, no ring-row, no feed; every view is a discovery event and every post is framed as 'putting this place on the map' (vs. Instagram's retrofitted, stale map and the inspiration artifact's top-of-list rings)

Geofence-verified capture makes every story proof-of-presence, so the story layer and the heat layer are the same data — heat that crowd-data utilities can't fake and competitors without a graph can't generate

Group-routed replies: a story's reply verbs are OMW and a group→group Pool invite, converting ephemeral content into nights out through the hero mechanic — no cold 1:1 DM surface for strangers, which is also the safety story
Nightlife-native 2-hour decay with visually legible cooling (vs. the 24h convention) — the map never lies about 'now'
Privacy by architecture: venue-anchored, never person-anchored; 18+, circle-default audiences, one-toggle Ghost Mode — sidestepping the exact backlash that hit Instagram Map 2025

Heat generated by the social layer compounds with network density — the intersection (crowd utility × friend map × group-first) that Current, NOITE, Jagat and Snap Map each hold only one or two corners of
risks: Ghost-town cold start is WORSE with ephemeral content (sparse posts also expire): must gate map regions on minimum liveness, backfill with venue baseline/events data, and use RSVP'd events as guaranteed content moments — launch neighbourhood-by-neighbourhood

Capture friction at midnight (dark, loud, drunk, phone at 20%): if the 2-tap composer still doesn't get posts, the ring layer dies; needs prompted moments and possibly early venue/promoter seeding, which then needs honest labelling

Heat gaming and venue self-promotion (staff hype-posting, ring farming): mitigations designed (caps, Vouch-weighting, labelled venue accounts) but unproven, and GPS spoofing/venue misattribution in dense districts like The Arches needs real geofence engineering

Moderation cost and duty of care: live 18+ nightlife video is the most expensive UGC to moderate, directly stressing riskiest-assumption #4 (unit economics at student price points); bystanders in clips raise consent issues face-blur only partly solves
OMW/en-route visibility could enable unwanted following if any gate slips — must remain strictly circle-gated, group-visible and covered by the women-first safety review before ship
Battery and background-location drain on a night out could make Func the app that kills your phone by 1am — needs a Zenly-style sleep-unless-watched location engine
prototypeScope: Buildable now in prototype/ (Expo + RN + react-native-svg, offline, in-memory): (1) new Story type in data/types.ts {id, venueId, groupId, authorId, ts (minutes-ago), audience: 'group'|'circles'|'city', frame: gradient-art spec + caption} with ~15 seeded flares in data/stories.ts weighted toward Arches venues; (2) VelmontMap.tsx: SVG segmented story-ring arcs on ringed venue pins (segment count = clips, opacity = recency) reusing the existing pulse animation budget from Decision 006; (3) venue mini-card gains a filmstrip of gradient story tiles (no photos exists — gradient frames match the monogram-avatar brand look) plus an en-route avatar row; (4) full-screen reel modal: auto-advancing gradient frames with caption, venue name, distance and cost chip persistent, reply bar with OMW (adds your avatar to en-route row, ticks the people counter), Pool us in (deep-links to Pool tab with a prefilled outgoing invite to that story's group — demo-able end-to-end with existing Pool state), and emoji hype; (5) closed-loop demo beat: after joining 'Neon Fridays @ Archive 9' in Events, a 'You're at Archive 9 — drop a flare' prompt posts a mock story that visibly brightens that pin's ring and heat on return to the map; (6) WorldMap.tsx: '38 flares live' added to the Velmont node label. Out of prototype scope: camera capture, real geofencing, decay timers (fake via seeded minutes-ago), moderation, Ghost Mode UI (copy line on Profile only). Fits the three-minute demo script as one new beat: Map → ringed pin → reel → 'Pool us in' → Pool tab."
